## Intended scope

This essay will introduce agent-based modeling (ABM) as a way of studying how macro-level economic patterns emerge from the interaction of heterogeneous, boundedly rational agents, and will discuss:

- What ABM adds relative to representative-agent or purely econometric approaches, and where it does not substitute for them.
- A simple, illustrative example of an agent-based model (to be developed, with code, once written).
- Connections to complex-systems concepts such as emergence, feedback, and path dependence.
- How this relates to coursework completed in 2026 in agent-based economic models (see the [CV](../../cv.qmd#academic-activities)).
